findings.evidence: no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile or .circleci/config.yml in the tracked tree
findings.remedy: add a workflow that runs the project's own test command on push
findings.title: Nothing runs the checks except a person remembering to

findings.detail: Fourteen ERR lines claim positioning and slogan drift across 7 files. Re-derived with `grep -Fc`: every one of the 7 files contains both strings exactly once. The gate is red because `rg` does not resolve inside a bash sub-shell, not because a document drifted. A reader following the message would edit correct documents.
findings.evidence: pnpm gates:docs -> exit 1; 'rg: command not found' x14; grep -Fc over all 7 required surfaces -> positioning=1 slogan=1 on each
findings.remedy: make the gate detect its own tool: fail with 'ripgrep not installed' when `command -v rg` is empty, or replace `rg -F -q` with `grep -F -q`, which is present everywhere the gate runs
findings.title: The docs gate fails on main, and the failure names the wrong cause

findings.detail: The two content checks are written as `if rg <pattern> <files>; then narrative_err; else narrative_ok; fi`. With `rg` absent the command exits 127, the else branch runs, and the gate prints 'ok: public surfaces contain no internal product-economics language' and 'ok: public product spelling is consistent'. Nothing was read. This is the project's own doctrine inverted: a zero-output failure rendered as a pass.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-narrative.sh:44 and :52; observed output carries both ok: lines directly under 'rg: command not found'
findings.remedy: guard the script on `command -v rg` before the first use and exit non-zero if it is absent; an `if <cmd>; then err; else ok; fi` shape must never be reachable with the command missing
findings.title: Two gate assertions print ok when the tool that would check them never ran

findings.detail: README:34 reads 'Status: architecture foundation' and :41 'the database, collectors, dashboard and agent runtime are not implemented yet'. Measured: 13 SQL migrations, an Electron app of 24 TypeScript source files, an MCP agent surface serving 7 tools, and 11 test suites that stand up a live Supabase and pass. README:79 says verification.md is 'Currently empty, and says so'; it holds 156 REQ rows across 22 families.
findings.evidence: git ls-files supabase/migrations | wc -l -> 13; grep -c '^| [A-Z]' docs/evidence/verification.md -> 156; pnpm -r test -> exit 0
findings.remedy: rewrite the status paragraph against the tree, and replace the verification.md row; the file is the first thing any reader or agent loads
findings.title: The README describes a project that stopped existing two months ago

findings.detail: The script exits 2 with 'ERROR: install jsonschema>=4.18'. Because gates:docs chains with && and check-docs.sh fails first, the composite never reaches it, so the breakage is invisible from the gate command. Five rows in the verification ledger cite this script as the check that was watched failing against a planted defect; that evidence cannot currently be reproduced.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/check-project-schemas.py -> exit 2; python3 -c 'import jsonschema' -> ModuleNotFoundError; grep -c check-project-schemas docs/evidence/verification.md -> 5
findings.remedy: pin the dependency where the gate can find it — a requirements file the gate installs from, or a uv/venv shim — and make the gate say which of 'no jsonschema' and 'schemas invalid' it hit
findings.title: The schema gate cannot run, and five verification rows name it as their verifier

findings.detail: 2,173 lines of React across 12 components. No test file imports the renderer, and the package declares no vitest, jsdom, testing-library or playwright. ProjectHome.tsx is 783 lines and the largest file in the app. What does cover it: tsc, and check-design.mjs on tokens and string keys — neither runs a component.
findings.evidence: cat apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/*.tsx | wc -l -> 2173; grep -rn renderer apps/desktop/test/ -> no match; grep -cE 'vitest|jsdom|testing-library|playwright' apps/desktop/package.json -> 0
findings.remedy: decide the renderer's verification story explicitly — a component harness, or a documented decision that the design gate plus typecheck is the whole contract; either is defensible, the current silence is not
findings.title: The half of the app a person actually touches has no tests

findings.detail: CO-093 — 'the bundle path has never been exercised by a real Claude Code session' — was resolved by handshake-e2e.test.mjs over a real PTY. That file is absent from the `test` script and self-skips unless FABRIC_E2E is set. A regression in the shipped CLI's mcp-session-id behaviour would reproduce CO-093 with nothing to catch it.
findings.evidence: node -e on package.json: scripts.test.includes('handshake-e2e') -> false; handshake-e2e.test.mjs:39 `if (!process.env.FABRIC_E2E)` -> skip
findings.remedy: run it in the default suite where the environment allows, or state in the carry-over row that CO-093 rests on a check nothing re-runs
findings.title: The check that closed the sharpest carry-over is not in the suite that runs

findings.detail: 93 rows, 65 reading `open`, 15 resolved. Three of the open ones are structural and named as such — CO-090 (same-uid isolation floor), CO-091 (the IPC bridge has no per-window authorisation, and all three BrowserWindows run sandbox:false), CO-092 (ORG1 hardcoded, runner assumed local). Those are filed risks, which is the right state; the finding is the ratio, not any single row.
findings.evidence: awk over the status column -> 65 open / 15 resolved / 93 total; apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts:726,745,759 -> sandbox: false
findings.remedy: age the rows: anything open across three runs is either scheduled, downgraded or closed as accepted risk. The audit's own ratchet counts survivals; the carry-over ledger does not
findings.title: Sixty-five open carry-overs, and the ledger has no drain

findings.detail: docs/brand/lint.py reports 0 errors and 130 B022 warnings, all of the form 'X is in the code with no registry row'. The app declares 166 keys. strings.md holds 11 table rows and states it covers 'the ones where the wording is a product decision rather than a label' — so the ratio may be intended; what is not stated is which side of that line the 130 fall on.
findings.evidence: python3 docs/brand/lint.py -> '0 error(s), 131 warning(s)', 130 of them B022; grep -c "^  '" i18n/en.ts -> 166; grep -cE '^\|' docs/brand/strings.md -> 11
findings.remedy: either agree the rows or narrow the contract to the strings that make a claim, and say which in strings.md — a 130-warning gate trains its reader to skip the output
findings.title: The brand gate is green by being advisory over four fifths of the interface

findings.detail: electron-vite emits index-*.js at 8,086.07 kB alongside separate chunks for abap, freemarker2, solidity, powerquery and two dozen other grammars. The app is an editor, so Monaco is deliberate; the full grammar set for a project workbench probably is not.
findings.remedy: measure before changing anything: if cold start is acceptable on the target machine this is a non-issue; if not, Monaco's language set is the first place to look
findings.title: One 8 MB renderer chunk, mostly language grammars nothing opens

findings.detail: docs/audit/ is the only entry in `git status --short`. .gitignore does not name it, so the next `git add -A` commits an audit report as if it were project documentation, and the run after that shows a diff nobody wrote.
findings.remedy: decide whether the report is committed evidence or local scratch, and record that in .gitignore either way
findings.title: The audit's own output is untracked and ungitignored
